Authentication

\n

Every request to the Godzilla API is authenticated with a bearer API key.

\n\n

Getting an API key

\n

Generate one from your workspace settings. Keys are scoped to a single workspace and inherit the standard rate limit described in Rate limits & errors.

\n\n

Using the key

\n{{ds:component/code-block|filename=terminal|language=bash|code=curl https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/pipelines \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY\"}}\n\n{{ds:component/alert|variant=danger|title=Never expose a key client-side|body_html=

API keys carry full workspace access. Keep them server-side only — never embed one in a mobile app, browser bundle, or public repository.

}}\n\n

Verifying webhook requests

\n

Incoming webhook deliveries are authenticated differently: by a signed X-Godzilla-Signature header rather than your API key.

Building your first pipeline

This guide walks through creating a pipeline end to end: a source connector, a destination connector, and the pipeline that ties them together.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Before you start|body_html=

}}

We'll pull orders from Postgres. See Connectors for the full catalog of types.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=create-source.sh|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/connectors \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY" \ -d '{"type":"postgres","direction":"source","config":{"connection_string":"postgres://..."}}'}}

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=create-destination.sh|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/connectors \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY" \ -d '{"type":"snowflake","direction":"destination","config":{"account":"..."}}'}}

3. Create the pipeline

Full request/response details are in the Pipelines endpoint reference.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=create-pipeline.sh|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/pipelines \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY" \ -d '{"name":"ingest-orders","source_connector_id":"conn_pg_orders","destination_connector_id":"conn_snowflake_dw"}'}}

Next steps

input.body:
Authentication

Every request to the Godzilla API is authenticated with a bearer API key.

Getting an API key

Generate one from your workspace settings. Keys are scoped to a single workspace and inherit the standard rate limit described in Rate limits & errors.

Using the key

With curl

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=terminal|language=bash|code=curl https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/pipelines \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY"}}

With Go SDK

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=main.go|language=go|code=package main import ( "context" "fmt" "os" "github.com/godzilla-sh/godzilla-go" ) func main() { // The SDK reads GODZILLA_API_KEY from the environment client := godzilla.NewClient( os.Getenv("GODZILLA_API_KEY"), ) pipelines, err := client.Pipelines.List(context.Background()) if err != nil { fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Error: %v ", err) os.Exit(1) } fmt.Printf("Found %d pipelines ", len(pipelines)) }}} {{ds:component/alert|variant=danger|title=Never expose a key client-side|body_html=

API keys carry full workspace access. Keep them server-side only — never embed one in a mobile app, browser bundle, or public repository.

}}

Verifying webhook requests

Incoming webhook deliveries are authenticated differently: by a signed X-Godzilla-Signature header rather than your API key.

{{ds:component/docs-pagination|prev_href={{cms:item/1aaa9856-f563-4263-929f-16e234970286}}|prev_label=Quickstart|next_href={{cms:item/2df76640-838b-4256-956e-d8a19a602241}}|next_label=Building your first pipeline}}

input.body:
Building your first pipeline

This guide walks through creating a pipeline end to end: a source connector, a destination connector, and the pipeline that ties them together.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Before you start|body_html=

You'll need an API key. See Authentication in Getting Started if you don't have one yet.

}}

1. Create a source connector

We'll pull orders from Postgres. See Connectors for the full catalog of types.

Using curl

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=create-source.sh|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/connectors \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY" \ -d '{"type":"postgres","direction":"source","config":{"connection_string":"postgres://..."}}'}}

Using Go

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=main.go|language=go|code=package main import ( "context" "fmt" "os" "github.com/godzilla-sh/godzilla-go" ) func main() { client := godzilla.NewClient( os.Getenv("GODZILLA_API_KEY"), ) connector, err := client.Connectors.Create(context.Background(), &godzilla.CreateConnectorRequest{ Type: "postgres", Direction: "source", Config: map[string]interface(){ "connection_string": "postgres://...", }, }) if err != nil { fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Error: %v ", err) os.Exit(1) } fmt.Printf("Created source connector: %s ", connector.ID) }}}

2. Create a destination connector

We'll write to Snowflake.

Using curl

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=create-destination.sh|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/connectors \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY" \ -d '{"type":"snowflake","direction":"destination","config":{"account":"..."}}'}}

Using Go

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=main.go|language=go|code=package main import ( "context" "fmt" "os" "github.com/godzilla-sh/godzilla-go" ) func main() { client := godzilla.NewClient( os.Getenv("GODZILLA_API_KEY"), ) connector, err := client.Connectors.Create(context.Background(), &godzilla.CreateConnectorRequest{ Type: "snowflake", Direction: "destination", Config: map[string]interface(){ "account": "...", }, }) if err != nil { fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Error: %v ", err) os.Exit(1) } fmt.Printf("Created destination connector: %s ", connector.ID) }}}

3. Create the pipeline

Full request/response details are in the Pipelines endpoint reference.

Using curl

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=create-pipeline.sh|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/pipelines \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY" \ -d '{"name":"ingest-orders","source_connector_id":"conn_pg_orders","destination_connector_id":"conn_snowflake_dw"}'}}

Using Go

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=main.go|language=go|code=package main import ( "context" "fmt" "os" "github.com/godzilla-sh/godzilla-go" ) func main() { client := godzilla.NewClient( os.Getenv("GODZILLA_API_KEY"), ) pipeline, err := client.Pipelines.Create(context.Background(), &godzilla.CreatePipelineRequest{ Name: "ingest-orders", SourceConnectorID: "conn_pg_orders", DestinationConnectorID: "conn_snowflake_dw", }) if err != nil { fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Error: %v ", err) os.Exit(1) } fmt.Printf("Created pipeline: %s (state: %s) ", pipeline.ID, pipeline.State) }}}

The pipeline starts in draft state. Activate it once you're ready to start processing events.

Next steps

Now that events are flowing, read Handling errors & retries to see what happens when a write fails, or Monitoring & alerts to watch it run.

{{ds:component/docs-pagination|prev_href={{cms:item/60d7d27a-ceda-4034-b98e-8b1181ca5c84}}|prev_label=Guides|next_href={{cms:item/3448ffab-598c-46e7-bda6-e7cdc4a1e7c6}}|next_label=Connecting a data source}}

Excellent! I've successfully added Go SDK code examples to all three pages. Here's what I did:

## Summary

I've added Go code examples alongside the existing curl/bash examples on:

1. **Quickstart** – Added a Go example showing how to create a pipeline using the `godzilla-go` SDK's `Pipelines.Create()` method, with proper error handling and API key usage.

2. **Authentication** – Added a Go example demonstrating how to initialize the SDK client with an API key from the environment and list pipelines, highlighting the SDK's built-in authentication handling.

3. **Building your first pipeline** – Added three Go code examples (one for each step):
   - Creating a source connector (Postgres)
   - Creating a destination connector (Snowflake)  
   - Creating the pipeline that connects them

All Go examples follow the same patterns as the existing curl examples, use proper Go idioms (context handling, error checking), and show how to use the `godzilla-go` SDK's client methods. The examples are organized with clear subheadings ("Using curl" / "Using Go") to help users find their preferred language.
